annotation.summary: Introduces the Transformer, a sequence-transduction architecture built entirely on self-attention, replacing recurrence and convolution. Demonstrates state-of-the-art results on English-to-German and English-to-French machine translation with substantially less training compute than prior recurrent models.
annotation.method: Encoder–decoder built from stacks of multi-head self-attention plus position-wise feed-forward layers, with sinusoidal positional encodings to preserve order. Trained on WMT 2014 with label smoothing and warm-up learning rate.
annotation.evaluation: Strong: cleanly motivates self-attention from a parallelism and path-length perspective; ablations on number of heads and dimensions are instructive. Weaker: positional encoding choice is presented as a fait accompli with limited comparison, and the analysis section is brief relative to the architectural contribution.
annotation.relevance: Foundational reference for anything we write about modern language models. Cite for the architectural baseline and for the parallelism argument.

highlights.quote: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
highlights.note: Worth quoting verbatim — this is the thesis sentence and easy to mis-paraphrase.

highlights.quote: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks…
highlights.note: Good background framing — pair with §1 of Bahdanau et al. 2015 when writing the related-work section.
